question: The railway system connecting St-Petersburg to Vladivostok is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Trans – Siberian Railways.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Trans-Siberian Railway connects Moscow to Vladivostok, running through St. Petersburg links and across Siberia to Russia's Far East. (ट्रांस-साइबेरियन रेलवे — रूस)

 

• It is the longest railway line in the world, with a total length of about 9,289 km, crossing 8 time zones.

 

• Construction was carried out between 1891 and 1916 under Tsar Alexander III and completed under Nicholas II.

 

• It connects European Russia with the Pacific coast, passing through major cities such as Yekaterinburg, Novosibirsk, Irkutsk (near Lake Baikal) and Khabarovsk.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Trans-Baikal Railway and the Amur Railway are historical sections that together form part of the larger Trans-Siberian network.

 

• Vladivostok, the eastern terminus, is Russia's principal Pacific port and the headquarters of the Russian Pacific Fleet.

 

NOTE

 

• The Altai Railway (Option 1): Not a recognised transcontinental Russian rail line connecting these two cities.

 

• The Amur Railways (Option 2): This is only one regional section (built 1908-1916) that forms part of the larger Trans-Siberian system, not the full St. Petersburg-Vladivostok line.

 

• Trans-Baikal Railway (Option 3): Similarly, this is only the section around Lake Baikal, part of the larger Trans-Siberian Railway, not the complete route itself.

question: As of 10 April 2022, who among the following is serving as the Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhupesh Baghel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhupesh Baghel of the Indian National Congress served as the Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh from 17 December 2018 to 13 December 2023, so he held the post as of 10 April 2022. (भूपेश बघेल — छत्तीसगढ़ के मुख्यमंत्री)

 

• He was the third Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, and led the state during the entire first Congress-led term after the 2018 assembly elections.

 

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000; Raipur is its capital.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• TS Singh Deo and Tamradhwaj Sahu were senior Congress ministers in the Baghel cabinet.

 

• Chhattisgarh's current (post-2023 election) Chief Minister is Vishnu Deo Sai of the BJP, who took office in December 2023, after this exam was held.

 

NOTE

 

• Kawasi Lakhma (Option 1): He was a minister for Excise and Commercial Tax in the Baghel government, not Chief Minister.

 

• Tamradhwaj Sahu (Option 2): He was the Home Minister in the Baghel cabinet, not Chief Minister.

 

• TS Singh Deo (Option 3): He was the Deputy Chief Minister/senior cabinet minister (Panchayat and Rural Development) under Baghel, not the Chief Minister himself.

question: The Electricity (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced in Lok Sabha on August 8, 2022. The Bill amends the Electricity Act established in _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2003.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Electricity (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 8 August 2022 to amend the Electricity Act, 2003. (विद्युत अधिनियम — 2003)

 

• The Electricity Act, 2003 consolidated laws relating to generation, transmission, distribution, trading and use of electricity in India, replacing earlier laws like the Indian Electricity Act, 1910.

 

• The 2022 amendment Bill primarily sought to allow multiple power distribution companies (discoms) to operate in the same area, promoting competition, and to strengthen provisions for renewable purchase obligations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Earlier amendments to the Electricity Act were made in 2003 itself and subsequently in 2007 for minor provisions, but the principal Act referred to in the 2022 Bill is the Electricity Act, 2003.

 

• The Ministry of Power is the nodal ministry responsible for the Act and its amendments.

 

NOTE

 

• 2005 (Option 1): No principal Electricity Act was enacted in this year.

 

• 2007 (Option 2): Not the year of the principal Act; only minor rule changes occurred around this time.

 

• 2001 (Option 3): The Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act existed earlier (1998), but the consolidated Electricity Act itself was passed in 2003, not 2001.

question: Which of the following sites is located on the hills near the Brahmaputra valley on the way to China and Myanmar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Daojali Hading.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Daojali Hading, in the North Cachar Hills of Assam, is an important Neolithic site located on hills near the Brahmaputra valley, on routes leading towards China and Myanmar. (दाओजाली हाडिंग — असम का नवपाषाणकालीन स्थल)

 

• Excavations there revealed polished stone tools (shouldered celts) and corded-ware pottery, similar to those found in South-East Asia and South China, suggesting cultural links along early migration/trade routes.

 

• It is regarded as evidence of the spread of Neolithic culture from South-East Asia into North-East India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important Neolithic sites of North-East India include Sarutaru (Assam) and Marakdola (Meghalaya).

 

• The Brahmaputra valley served as a natural corridor linking the Indian subcontinent with South-East Asia and China.

 

NOTE

 

• Mehrgarh (Option 1): A Neolithic/Chalcolithic site in Balochistan, Pakistan, considered a precursor to the Indus Valley Civilisation, unrelated to the Brahmaputra valley.

 

• Paiyampalli (Option 2): A Neolithic-Megalithic site in Tamil Nadu, in South India, not near the Brahmaputra.

 

• Gufkral (Option 3): A Neolithic site in Kashmir, in the north-west of India, not on the route to China/Myanmar.

question: With which of the following states is the folk dance Tarangmel associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tarangmel (also spelt Tarangamel) is a traditional folk dance of Goa, performed by groups of dancers carrying colourful taranga (decorated flags/banners on bamboo poles). (तरंगमेल नृत्य — गोवा)

 

• It is typically performed during the Shigmo (Shigmotsav) festival, Goa's version of Holi, as part of religious and cultural processions.

 

• Dancers move in coordinated formations to the beat of traditional percussion instruments like the dhol and taasha, symbolising joy and communal celebration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Goa include Fugdi, Dhalo, Dekhni and Corridinho.

 

• Goa's Shigmo festival features vibrant folk-dance parades (Shigmo floats) across towns like Panaji and Margao.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): Known for folk dances such as Karma, Saila and Matki, not Tarangmel.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Known for Karagattam, Bharatanatyam and Kolattam, not Tarangmel.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Known for Theyyam, Kaikottikali and Thiruvathirakali, not Tarangmel.

question: Distance covered by object is ______ to time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is directly proportional.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For an object moving at constant (uniform) speed, the distance covered is directly proportional to time, expressed as Distance = Speed × Time. (दूरी — समय के अनुक्रमानुपाती)

 

• 'Directly proportional' means that as time increases, distance also increases in the same ratio, provided speed remains constant.

 

• This relationship, s ∝ t, forms the basis of the equations of uniform motion studied in kinematics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• For uniformly accelerated motion starting from rest, distance is proportional to the square of time (s ∝ t²), not directly proportional.

 

• Speed itself is defined as the rate of change of distance with time (Speed = Distance/Time).

 

NOTE

 

• Equal proportional (Option 1): Not a standard term used to describe this physical relationship.

 

• Inversely proportional (Option 3): Inverse proportionality would mean distance decreases as time increases, which is not true for an object moving at constant speed.

 

• Double proportional (Option 4): Not a recognised or standard term in kinematics.

question: The ‘Family Doctor’ programme launched on a pilot basis in the first week of September 2022. This programme was launched by which state government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Family Doctor' concept/programme was launched by the Government of Andhra Pradesh on a pilot basis in the first week of September 2022, under the leadership of Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy. (फैमिली डॉक्टर योजना — आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• The programme was designed to provide doorstep primary healthcare by sending teams of doctors to visit YSR Village/Ward Health Clinics twice a month to attend to rural patients.

 

• It builds on Andhra Pradesh's existing network of YSR Village Health Clinics (YVHCs), aiming to improve access to healthcare in remote and rural areas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Andhra Pradesh's health initiatives also include the YSR Aarogyasri scheme for cashless health insurance and 104/108 ambulance services.

 

• The programme was later scaled up statewide after the successful pilot phase.

 

NOTE

 

• Haryana (Option 1): Did not launch this specific 'Family Doctor' pilot programme in September 2022.

 

• Odisha (Option 2): Known for schemes like Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana, not this Family Doctor pilot.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Known for the Makkalai Thedi Maruthuvam doorstep healthcare scheme, a separate initiative, not this programme.

question: Which of the following facts is NOT associated with PC Mahalanobis who contributed to the formulation of India’s Five Year Plans?
option_1: He established the Indian Statistical Institute.
option_3: He is known as the architect of Indian planning.
option_4: Mahalanobis was born in 1983 in Calcutta.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahalanobis was born in 1983 in Calcutta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis was actually born on 29 June 1893 in Calcutta, not 1983 — the year 1983 mentioned in this option is factually wrong, making it the statement NOT associated with him. (पी.सी. महालनोबिस — जन्म 1893)

 

• He founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Kolkata in 1931.

 

• He started the journal Sankhya: The Indian Journal of Statistics in 1933, and developed the Mahalanobis Distance statistical measure.

 

• He is regarded as the architect of the Second Five Year Plan and is known as the 'Father of Indian statistics'; he also chaired the Planning Commission's Perspective Planning Division.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahalanobis received the Padma Vibhushan in 1968 and passed away on 28 June 1972.

 

• The Mahalanobis Model, used in the Second Five Year Plan (1956-61), emphasised rapid industrialisation with focus on heavy/basic industries.

 

NOTE

 

• He established the Indian Statistical Institute (Option 1): This is a true, correctly associated fact.

 

• He started the journal Sankhya (Option 2): This is a true, correctly associated fact.

 

• He is known as the architect of Indian planning (Option 3): This is a true, correctly associated fact.

question: The Winter Youth Olympic Games 2024 will be held in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gangwon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2024 Winter Youth Olympic Games were held in Gangwon Province, South Korea, from 19 to 1 February 2024, making South Korea the first Asian country to host a Winter Youth Olympics. (गंगवोन शीतकालीन युवा ओलंपिक 2024 — दक्षिण कोरिया)

 

• Gangwon had earlier hosted parts of the 2018 Winter Olympics (PyeongChang 2018), so existing winter-sports infrastructure was reused.

 

• The Games featured youth athletes (aged roughly 15-18) competing across various winter sports disciplines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2020 Winter Youth Olympics were held in Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

• The 2026 Summer Youth Olympics are scheduled to be held in Dakar, Senegal (postponed from 2022), while Singapore hosted the first-ever Summer Youth Olympics in 2010.

 

NOTE

 

• Lausanne (Option 2): This was the host of the 2020 Winter Youth Olympic Games, not 2024.

 

• Dakar (Option 3): This is the host city for the upcoming Summer Youth Olympic Games (2026), a different (summer) edition.

 

• Singapore (Option 4): This hosted the inaugural 2010 Summer Youth Olympic Games, not the 2024 Winter edition.

question: “All India Muslim League” was established in 1906 at ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dacca.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The All India Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 in Dacca (now Dhaka, Bangladesh), under the leadership of Nawab Salimullah Khan, following the Simla Deputation of 1906. (मुस्लिम लीग की स्थापना — ढाका, 1906)

 

• Its founding aim included protecting the political rights and interests of Muslims in British India and promoting loyalty to the British government.

 

• The League later played a central role in the demand for Pakistan, especially after adopting the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aga Khan III was the League's first (honorary) president.

 

• The League's formation followed closely after the Simla Deputation (1906), where Muslim leaders sought separate electorates from Viceroy Lord Minto.

 

NOTE

 

• Bombay (Option 2): The Indian National Congress held several sessions here, including its founding session in 1885, but not the Muslim League's founding.

 

• Madras (Option 3): Not the founding location of the Muslim League.

 

• Surat (Option 4): Known for the 1907 Congress split between Moderates and Extremists, not the founding of the Muslim League.

question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Right to Vote.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to Vote is a constitutional/legal right granted under Article 326 of the Constitution and the Representation of the People Act, 1951, not a Fundamental Right under Part III. (मतदान का अधिकार — संवैधानिक अधिकार, मौलिक अधिकार नहीं)

 

• Part III of the Indian Constitution guarantees six Fundamental Rights: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 

• The Supreme Court has held that the right to vote, while important for democracy, is a statutory right, not a Fundamental Right.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Right to Property was also removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) and made a legal right under Article 300A.

 

• The Right to Education (Article 21A) was added as a Fundamental Right by the 86th Amendment (2002).

 

NOTE

 

• Right to Freedom of Religion (Option 1): A Fundamental Right under Articles 25-28 of Part III.

 

• Right against Exploitation (Option 2): A Fundamental Right under Articles 23-24 of Part III.

 

• Right to Equality (Option 3): A Fundamental Right under Articles 14-18 of Part III.

question: The Trimbakeshwar is the origin of which of the following rivers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Godavari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Godavari River originates near Trimbakeshwar in the Western Ghats (Sahyadri range), in Nashik district, Maharashtra. (त्र्यंबकेश्वर — गोदावरी नदी का उद्गम)

 

• The Godavari is the second-longest river in India (after the Ganga) and the largest river system of peninsular India, often called the 'Dakshin Ganga'.

 

• It flows eastward across Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh (and touches Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Karnataka, Puducherry) before draining into the Bay of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Trimbakeshwar is also famous for the Trimbakeshwar Shiva Temple, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas.

 

• The Kumbh Mela is held at Nashik-Trimbakeshwar on the banks of the Godavari, once every 12 years.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahanadi (Option 1): Originates near Sihawa, Chhattisgarh, not Trimbakeshwar.

 

• Tapti (Option 2): Originates from the Satpura Range near Multai, Madhya Pradesh, not Trimbakeshwar.

 

• Ravi (Option 3): Originates in the Himalayas near Rohtang Pass, Himachal Pradesh, not Trimbakeshwar.

question: Who among the following was the guru of Pandit Ravi Shankar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Allaudin Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Allauddin Khan (of the Maihar gharana) was the guru of the legendary sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar. (उस्ताद अलाउद्दीन खान — पंडित रविशंकर के गुरु)

 

• Allauddin Khan trained Ravi Shankar in sitar and Hindustani classical music at Maihar; Ravi Shankar later became one of the most influential Indian classical musicians globally.

 

• Allauddin Khan was also a renowned sarod player, and was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1971.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ravi Shankar's other guru-siblings under Allauddin Khan included his own son Ali Akbar Khan (sarod) and daughter Annapurna Devi, whom Ravi Shankar later married.

 

• Ravi Shankar was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999 and composed the score for films like Satyajit Ray's Apu Trilogy.

 

NOTE

 

• Bismillah Khan (Option 1): A legendary shehnai player, Bharat Ratna awardee, not Ravi Shankar's guru.

 

• Amjad Ali Khan (Option 2): A renowned sarod player belonging to the Senia Bangash gharana, not Ravi Shankar's guru.

 

• Ali Akbar Khan (Option 3): A celebrated sarod player and Allauddin Khan's son (Ravi Shankar's brother-in-law/fellow disciple), not his guru.

question:
Match Column-A with Column-B.

Column-A (Vitamin): i. Vitamin A, ii. Vitamin B12, iii. Vitamin C, iv. Vitamin D

Alternative name: a. Ascorbic acid, b. Retinol, c. Cobalamin, d. Ergocalciferol
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-b, ii-c, iii-a, iv-d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct matching is: Vitamin A = Retinol, Vitamin B12 = Cobalamin, Vitamin C = Ascorbic acid, Vitamin D = Ergocalciferol. (विटामिन के वैकल्पिक नाम — रेटिनॉल, कोबालामिन, एस्कॉर्बिक एसिड, एर्गोकैल्सिफेरॉल)

 

• Vitamin A (Retinol) is essential for vision and immune function; its deficiency causes night blindness.

 

• Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) is essential for red blood cell formation and nerve function; deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.

 

• Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) is an antioxidant important for collagen synthesis; deficiency causes scurvy.

 

• Vitamin D (Ergocalciferol/Cholecalciferol) is essential for calcium absorption and bone health; deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vitamin D2 is called Ergocalciferol (plant-derived) while Vitamin D3 is called Cholecalciferol (synthesised in skin from sunlight).

 

• Vitamin E is known as Tocopherol and Vitamin K as Phylloquinone/Menadione.

 

NOTE

 

• i-b, ii-a, iii-c, iv-d (Option 1): Incorrectly swaps the alternative names for Vitamin B12 and Vitamin C.

 

• i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d (Option 2): Incorrectly swaps the alternative names for Vitamin A and Vitamin B12.

 

• i-c, ii-b, iii-d, iv-a (Option 3): Incorrectly matches all four vitamins to the wrong alternative names except position pattern; the correct chemical names are not assigned to the right vitamins.

question: In AIBA Boxing Junior Boys and Girls Competitions, the bouts must consist of each round of ____ minutes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 min.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per AIBA (now IBA) Technical and Competition Rules, in Junior Boys and Girls competitions, bouts consist of 3 rounds of 2 minutes each, with a 1-minute rest between rounds. (एआईबीए जूनियर मुक्केबाजी — प्रत्येक राउंड 2 मिनट)

 

• AIBA (International Boxing Association), now rebranded as IBA, is the world governing body for amateur (Olympic-style) boxing.

 

• Different age categories have different round durations — junior categories use shorter rounds compared to elite/senior categories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• In Elite (Senior) men's/women's competitions, bouts typically consist of 3 rounds of 3 minutes each.

 

• IBA headquarters is located in Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

NOTE

 

• 5 min (Option 1): Not the round duration for any standard AIBA/IBA amateur boxing category.

 

• 3 min (Option 2): This is the round duration for Elite (Senior) competitions, not Junior.

 

• 1 min (Option 3): Too short to be a competition round duration under AIBA/IBA rules; 1 minute is instead the standard rest period between rounds.

question: Which of the following river rises in the Indian Himalayan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yamuna.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Yamuna River originates from the Yamunotri Glacier on the slopes of Bandarpunch peak in the Indian Himalayas (Uttarakhand). (यमुना नदी — यमुनोत्री हिमनद, उत्तराखंड)

 

• It is the largest tributary of the Ganga, flowing through Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, and Uttar Pradesh before merging with the Ganga at Prayagraj (Allahabad).

 

• Unlike the Yamuna, several major Himalayan rivers in North India actually rise beyond Indian territory, in Nepal or Tibet, before entering India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Important tributaries of the Yamuna include the Chambal, Betwa, Ken and Sindh.

 

• The Yamuna basin drains a large part of the Indo-Gangetic Plain in North India.

 

NOTE

 

• Kosi (Option 1): Rises in Tibet (as the Sun Kosi/Arun and other tributaries join in Nepal) before entering Bihar, India.

 

• Gandak (Option 3): Rises in the Nepal Himalayas (near the Tibet border), not within Indian territory.

 

• Ghaghra (Option 4): Rises in Tibet, near Lake Manasarovar, before flowing through Nepal into India.

question: Which of the following town was built by the ruler Vijayalaya in Kaveri delta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thanjavur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vijayalaya, the founder of the imperial Chola dynasty, captured and built up Thanjavur around 850 CE in the fertile Kaveri delta, making it the Chola capital. (विजयालय चोल — तंजावुर की स्थापना)

 

• Vijayalaya seized Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars, laying the foundation for the resurgence of Chola power in South India.

 

• Thanjavur later flourished as a major cultural and administrative centre, especially under Raja Raja Chola I, who built the famous Brihadeeswarar Temple there.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brihadeeswarar Temple at Thanjavur, built by Raja Raja Chola I (c. 1010 CE), is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and part of the 'Great Living Chola Temples'.

 

• The Chola dynasty later extended its capital influence to Gangaikonda Cholapuram under Rajendra Chola I.

 

NOTE

 

• Tiruchirappalli (Option 1): An ancient city with Rock Fort Temple, but not founded by Vijayalaya.

 

• Tiruppur (Option 2): Known today as a textile hub, unrelated to Vijayalaya's founding.

 

• Madurai (Option 3): The historic capital of the Pandya dynasty, not associated with Vijayalaya or the Cholas' founding.

question: The first complete census taken in India is in the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1881.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first complete, synchronous census of India was conducted in 1881 under Lord Ripon, covering almost the entire country in a single operation. (भारत की प्रथम संपूर्ण जनगणना — 1881)

 

• Census operations have since been conducted every 10 years without interruption, making the Indian census one of the largest administrative exercises in the world.

 

• The 1881 census marked the beginning of a regular decennial census system continued to the present (the last conducted census was in 2011).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A non-synchronous trial census was attempted earlier in 1872 under Lord Mayo, but it was not conducted uniformly across all regions at the same time, so it is not counted as the first 'complete' census.

 

• The Census of India is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 

NOTE

 

• 1872 (Option 2): This was the first *attempted* census, but non-synchronous and incomplete, not the first 'complete' census.

 

• 1900 (Option 3): Not a census year; censuses are conducted in years ending in 1 (e.g., 1881, 1891, 1901).

 

• 1860 (Option 4): No census, complete or partial, was conducted in this year.

question: Which of the following is NOT the function of the central bank of the country?
option_1: It controls money supply of the country.
option_2: It acts as a banker to the government.
option_3: It accepts deposits from the public.
option_4: It issues the currency of the country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It accepts deposits from the public.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A central bank (such as the Reserve Bank of India) does not deal directly with the general public by accepting deposits — that is the role of commercial banks. (केंद्रीय बैंक — जनता से जमा नहीं लेता)

 

• The central bank instead acts as the 'banker's bank', holding reserves of and lending to commercial banks, and it is the banker to the government, managing government accounts and public debt.

 

• Core functions of a central bank include being the sole note-issuing authority, controlling the money supply and credit through monetary policy, and acting as lender of last resort.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and was nationalised in 1949.

 

• The RBI's monetary policy tools include Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, CRR, SLR and Open Market Operations.

 

NOTE

 

• It controls money supply of the country (Option 1): This is a genuine, correctly associated function of a central bank (via monetary policy).

 

• It acts as a banker to the government (Option 2): This is a genuine, correctly associated function of a central bank.

 

• It issues the currency of the country (Option 4): This is a genuine, correctly associated function — the central bank has the sole right to issue currency notes.

question: The ‘Rann Utsav’ is organised in which of the following states of India to promote tourism?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rann Utsav is an annual cultural festival organised in the Great Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, to promote tourism, typically held from around November to February. (रण उत्सव — कच्छ, गुजरात)

 

• It showcases Gujarat's handicrafts, folk music, folk dance, cuisine and the white salt desert landscape, with tent-city accommodations at Dhordo village.

 

• The festival was launched to boost tourism in the Kutch region after the 2001 Gujarat earthquake and has since become a major tourist attraction, especially around the full moon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dhordo village, near the Rann Utsav venue, was awarded the UN World Tourism Organization's 'Best Tourism Village' title in 2023.

 

• The Great Rann of Kutch is one of the largest salt deserts in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan (Option 2): Known for its own festivals like the Pushkar Fair and Desert Festival (Jaisalmer), not the Rann Utsav.

 

• Punjab (Option 3): Known for festivals like Baisakhi, not the Rann Utsav.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Known for festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi, not the Rann Utsav.

question: Which of the following states has got first of its kind state-level bird atlas in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kerala Bird Atlas (KBA), released in 2022, is India's first-ever state-level, scientifically rigorous bird atlas, and is also described as Asia's largest bird atlas. (केरल बर्ड एटलस — भारत का पहला राज्य-स्तरीय पक्षी एटलस)

 

• It was compiled through a citizen-science survey covering the entire state of Kerala over multiple seasons, involving over a thousand birdwatchers.

 

• The atlas systematically documents the distribution, abundance and seasonal patterns of bird species across Kerala's grids, providing a scientific baseline for conservation planning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

• The project was coordinated by organisations including Bird Count India, Kerala Forest Department, and SACON (Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History).

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala is also known for other biodiversity/conservation firsts, such as being among the earliest states to conduct dedicated bird surveys.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Has not produced the first state-level bird atlas of this kind.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 3): Not associated with India's first state-level bird atlas.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 4): Not associated with India's first state-level bird atlas.

question: Identify the correct statement about inertia.
option_1: Greater the mass, greater the inertia
option_2: Lesser the weight, greater the inertia
option_3: Lesser the mass, greater the inertia
option_4: Greater the mass, lesser the inertia
solution_text:
The correct answer is Greater the mass, greater the inertia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Inertia is the natural tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or uniform motion, and it is directly proportional to the mass of the body. (जड़त्व — द्रव्यमान के अनुक्रमानुपाती)

 

• This means an object with greater mass has greater inertia, requiring a larger force to change its state of motion; a lighter object is easier to accelerate or stop.

 

• Mass is, in fact, often defined physically as a quantitative measure of inertia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newton's First Law of Motion (the Law of Inertia) states that a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.

 

• Inertia has three types: inertia of rest, inertia of motion, and inertia of direction.

 

NOTE

 

• Lesser the weight, greater the inertia (Option 2): Incorrect — inertia depends on mass, not weight, and the relationship stated is also inverted.

 

• Lesser the mass, greater the inertia (Option 3): Incorrect — this reverses the true direct relationship between mass and inertia.

 

• Greater the mass, lesser the inertia (Option 4): Incorrect — this also reverses the true direct relationship between mass and inertia.

question: The Anantraj Sagar Tank was built by the ______ rulers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vijayanagara.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Anantraj Sagar Tank was built by the Vijayanagara rulers, constructed using a long earthen dam across the Maldevi river, as part of large-scale water storage infrastructure. (अनंतराज सागर टैंक — विजयनगर शासक)

 

• The Vijayanagara Empire (1336-1646 CE), based in present-day Karnataka, took special interest in building large and small irrigation tanks to support agriculture in the semi-arid Deccan region.

 

• Such tanks reflect the empire's sophisticated water-management and irrigation engineering achievements, complementing the well-known stepwells and canal systems of the era.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vijayanagara Empire's capital, Hampi, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring extensive irrigation canals from the Tungabhadra river.

 

• Notable Vijayanagara rulers include Harihara I, Bukka Raya I, and Krishnadevaraya.

 

NOTE

 

• Maratha (Option 2): Known for forts and administrative reforms under Shivaji and later Peshwas, not this tank.

 

• Pala (Option 3): A dynasty of eastern India (Bengal-Bihar region) known for patronage of Buddhism, not associated with this tank.

 

• Chola (Option 4): Known for temple tanks and irrigation works in Tamil Nadu (e.g., the Kaveri delta), but the Anantraj Sagar Tank specifically is attributed to the Vijayanagara rulers, not the Cholas.

question: Who among the following choreographers from Bollywood was a three time National Award winner in 2003, 2007 and 2009? He/She worked in many Hindi movies including Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s movie ‘Devdas’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saroj Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saroj Khan was a legendary Bollywood choreographer and the first choreographer to win three National Film Awards for Best Choreography, including for her work on Sanjay Leela Bhansali's 'Devdas' (2002). (सरोज खान — प्रसिद्ध कोरियोग्राफर, तीन राष्ट्रीय पुरस्कार)

 

• She choreographed some of Hindi cinema's most iconic songs, including 'Dola Re Dola' (Devdas), and worked extensively with actresses like Madhuri Dixit and Sridevi.

 

• She began her career as a child dancer/background dancer and rose to become one of the most influential and highest-paid choreographers in the Indian film industry, earning the title 'Master Ji'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Saroj Khan was honoured with the Padma Shri nomination discussions over her career and received several Filmfare Awards for Best Choreography.

 

• She passed away in July 2020.

 

NOTE

 

• Geeta Kapoor (Option 1): A well-known dance reality-show judge/choreographer, but not the three-time National Award winner referenced here.

 

• Farah Khan (Option 3): A prominent choreographer-turned-director (known for films like 'Om Shanti Om'), but not associated with these specific three National Awards for Devdas-era choreography.

 

• Vaibhavi Merchant (Option 4): A noted choreographer (e.g., for 'Bunty Aur Babli'), but not the specific three-time National Award winner described in this question.

question: In what form is the energy derived from the food that we eat is stored in our body?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Glycogen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The energy derived from digested food is stored in the human body mainly in the form of Glycogen, a highly branched polysaccharide made of glucose units. (ग्लाइकोजन — शरीर में ऊर्जा का संग्रहित रूप)

 

• Glycogen is stored primarily in the liver and skeletal muscles; liver glycogen helps maintain blood glucose levels, while muscle glycogen provides energy for muscular activity.

 

• When the body needs energy, glycogen is broken down (glycogenolysis) back into glucose, which is then used in cellular respiration to release energy (as ATP).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Excess energy beyond glycogen storage capacity is stored in the body as fat (triglycerides) in adipose tissue.

 

• Insulin promotes glycogen synthesis (glycogenesis), while glucagon and adrenaline promote its breakdown.

 

NOTE

 

• Maltose (Option 1): A disaccharide formed from two glucose units, mainly a digestive intermediate, not the body's storage form of energy.

 

• Glucose (Option 2): The primary transportable form of sugar used directly for immediate energy, but it is not the storage form — it is converted to and stored as glycogen.

 

• Starch (Option 4): The storage form of carbohydrate energy in plants, not in the human/animal body.
